# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 43 (Bu-Vb Pc43)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc43  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 43  
**Title (English, from literature):** Intruding on a lustful couple  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 43 (also known as the *Sabhojanasikkhāpada*) is an expiation rule within the Vinaya Piṭaka of the Theravāda tradition. The rule provides that a monk who intrudes and sits down uninvited in a household during meals or intimate relations (*yo pana bhikkhu sabhojane kule anupakhajja nisajjam kappeyya, pācittiyan ti*; Vin IV 95) commits a *pācittiya* offense requiring confession [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
